brief:
A federal judge on Monday barred the Trump administration from punishing Americans who share evidence with the International Criminal Court or work with UN experts and Palestinian human rights groups, Democracy for the Arab World Now reported. The ruling blocked penalties against those collaborating with sanctioned organizations alongside the ICC.

The case was brought by DAWN and the Taxpayers Alliance Against Genocide, which had themselves been sanctioned by the administration. The decision prevents the government from retaliating against citizens engaging with the court or the rights groups over their advocacy work.
dek: (New York, November 24, 2026) - A federal judge on Monday barred the Trump administration from punishing Americans for sharing evidence with the International Criminal Court (ICC), or for working with the UN expert and Palestinian human rights groups sanctioned alongside it, Democracy for the Arab World Now (DAWN) and Taxpayers Alliance Against Genocide (TAAG), the plaintiffs in the suit, said today.
title: Judge blocks Trump from punishing ICC advocacy by Americans
